content.title: About
content.content: Light Italian dressing is a blend of vegetable oils, vinegar, lemon juice, spices and herbs such as oregano, basil and garlic. It offers a bright aroma, moderate acidity and low calorie content, making it popular for salads and marinades.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Italian dressing originated in the United States in the early 20th century as an adaptation of traditional Mediterranean flavors.
The light version typically contains 30–40 % oil, with the remainder made up of vinegar, lemon juice and flavorings.
The herbs used in the dressing have antioxidant properties.
In the US the dressing is commonly sold in 250–500 ml bottles.
There are many variations, including mustard, honey or dried vegetable powders.

items.title: Low calorie density
items.content: Light dressing provides roughly 50–70 kcal per tablespoon, allowing generous use without significantly raising the energy content of meals.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Herbs and spices (oregano, basil, garlic) contain polyphenols that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: When olive oil is part of the formula, the dressing can improve lipid profiles thanks to its monounsaturated fats.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: Vinegar and lemon juice stimulate gastric juice production, enhancing nutrient absorption.

items.title: Source of vitamin E
items.content: The vegetable oils supply vitamin E, a potent antioxidant.

items.title: Allergy to ingredients
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to mustard, garlic or specific oils.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Certain commercial versions contain higher levels of salt, which may be unsuitable for people with hypertension.

items.title: Acidity
items.content: The high acidity of vinegar can irritate the stomach lining in people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Preservatives
items.content: Commercial products may include preservatives such as potassium sorbate, which can cause sensitivity in some consumers.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: Light Italian dressing can be tossed with green or vegetable salads, used as a marinade for chicken, fish or tofu, and added to roasted vegetables or pasta for extra flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the dressing in a tightly sealed bottle in the refrigerator. Once opened, it typically remains good for 2–3 months. Discard if the smell, color or taste changes.
